title: Collect VCF Operations for Networks inventory across token refreshes
prompt:
Our fleet-inventory service needs to pull the application inventory out of a VCF Operations for Networks appliance (VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1, the successor to vRealize Network Insight). The Go module skeleton is in place. `internal/opsnet` is the client and none of it is implemented yet.

Implement `internal/opsnet` so that `Client.CollectInventory` logs in, walks every page of the application list, fetches the detail record for each listed application, and `Client.Close` hands the auth token back.

The awkward part is the token. Auth tokens on this API are short-lived and the appliance returns the expiry along with the token, so a collection over a decent-sized inventory routinely outlives the token it started with. When the token dies part way through the run the client has to pick up a fresh one and carry on from exactly where it was: no page that already came back may be fetched a second time, and nothing already collected may be dropped. Detail fetches run concurrently, so several in-flight requests can discover the same dead token at the same moment - they must end up sharing one replacement rather than each minting their own. Tokens are a limited resource too (the appliance caps how many a single user may hold at once), so don't burn them, and don't retry into a loop against an appliance that is rejecting every token you ask for.

`docs/contract.json` is the wire contract for the four operations in scope, and `docs/official_sources.json` records which revision of the API specification it was derived from. Follow the contract exactly. In particular: an optional query parameter or request body property that the caller has not set must not appear on the wire at all - not as `cursor=`, not as `modifiedAfter=0`, not as `fetch_member_counts=false`, not as `"value": ""`.

Everything you need in order to check your work is already in the repo. `go test -race ./...` drives the client against a loopback mock of the contract and asserts the shape of every request it puts on the wire. Leave `internal/opsnetmock/`, `verify/` and `docs/` alone - they are the harness, not the deliverable.
deliverable: A working implementation of internal/opsnet (Client, New, CollectInventory, Close, TokenCreates) that satisfies docs/contract.json.

environment.notes: The module has no third-party requirements, so the suite runs with GOPROXY=off.

what_is_checked: Exact request wire shape per operation: method, path (including the /api/ni base path from the specification), Authorization header format `NetworkInsight {token}`, Content-Type, and the exact set of query parameters and request body properties present.

Unset optional fields are absent from the wire rather than sent empty: no `cursor=` on the first page, no `modifiedAfter`, no `fetch_member_counts=false`, no `"value": ""` inside the Domain object, and no `domain` object at all when no domain is configured.
operationId `create` carries no Authorization header, because the operation declares `security: []` in the specification.

Token refresh loses no work: a page that already succeeded is never refetched, a page that failed on an expired token is retried from the same cursor rather than restarting pagination, and every listed application is fetched exactly once.
Concurrent detail fetches that all hit 401 collapse onto a single call to operationId `create`; a worker that finds the token already replaced reuses the replacement.
Proactive refresh reads Token.expiry as epoch milliseconds, so a token is replaced before it expires and no 401 is ever served.
At most one refresh per request: an appliance that rejects every token produces an error rather than an unbounded retry loop.
Results keep the pagination order regardless of the order concurrent detail responses arrive in, and `go test -race` reports no data race.
The mock's route table matches docs/contract.json exactly, and docs/official_sources.json records the specification path, a 40-character commit sha and every operationId in the contract.
verification.no_live_endpoints: The suite talks only to an in-process HTTP server bound to 127.0.0.1 by internal/opsnetmock. Nothing contacts a VMware endpoint.
